skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. verus! {
2. 
3. // `PAGE_ALIGNMENT` is an external (arch-crate) constant. Model it so that verified
4. // exec code referencing it has a Verus specification. The page alignment's numeric
5. // value is the page size (both are 4096 on the supported target), which is the link
6. // that lets `from_address` relate `is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)` to `spec_page_size()`.
7. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::PAGE_ALIGNMENT ] -> (result: Alignment)
8.     ensures
9.         ::sys::mm::spec_align_value(result) == spec_page_size(),
10. ;
11. 
12. // Success condition for the validating constructor, stated purely on the abstract
13. // address value. `from_address` validates, it does NOT normalize: success requires the
14. // *input* to already be page-aligned.
15. pub open spec fn spec_aligned(addr_view: int) -> bool {
16.     addr_view % spec_page_size() == 0
17. }
18. 
19. } // verus!
20.

1. ## Response to Turn 1
2. 
3. ### What I Changed
4. 
5. The reviewer's FAIL was: `from_address` (page.rs) carried `proof! { admit(); }`, so its
6. `ensures` passed vacuously. Root cause: the `Address::is_aligned` trait method had **no
7. spec**, so `addr.is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)? == true` could not be related back to
8. `addr@ % spec_page_size() == 0`. I added the missing dependency specs and removed the
9. `admit`, then re-proved `from_address` (it now discharges automatically).
10. 
11. 1. **`src/libs/sys/src/sys/mm/alignment.rs`** (new spec fn, ~lines 147–185, in a
12.    `#[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)] verus! { }` block):
13.    - Added `pub open spec fn spec_align_value(align: Alignment) -> int` — a faithful,
14.      concrete `match` mapping each `Alignment` variant to its byte value (`Align4 => 4`,
15.      …, `Align4096 => 4096`, …). This is the "spec accessor mapping an `Alignment` to its
16.      `int` value" the reviewer asked for. Concrete (not `uninterp`), so it is a real
17.      definition, not added trust surface.
18. 
19. 2. **`src/libs/sys/src/sys/mm/address/mod.rs`** (spec on the trait declaration, ~line 102):
20.    - Added to `fn is_aligned(&self, align: Alignment) -> Result<bool, Error>`:
21.      ```rust
22.      #[verus_spec(result =>
23.          ensures
24.              result matches Ok(aligned)
25.                  && aligned == (self@ % crate::mm::spec_align_value(align) == 0),
26.      )]
27.      ```
28.    - This relates the boolean result to the abstract address value (`self@`) and the
29.      alignment's value. `self@` is available via the `Address: View<V = int>` supertrait.
30.    - **Strengthening vs. the reviewer's literal suggestion:** I made the result `Ok`
31.      (`result matches Ok(aligned) && …`) rather than leaving `Err` unconstrained
32.      (`Err(_) => true`). This is *required* for `from_address`'s `Err => !spec_aligned(addr@)`
33.      to hold: if `is_aligned` could return `Err`, `from_address` could propagate `Err` for an
34.      *aligned* input, violating its (unchanged) `ensures`. The strengthening is faithful —
35.      every concrete impl always returns `Ok` (`VirtualAddress`/`PhysicalAddress` wrap in
36.      `Ok(...)`; `PageAligned`/`PageTableAligned` delegate to those). No `Address` impl is
37.      `#[verus_verify]`, so this is a trusted contract that no impl is forced to re-prove.
38. 
39. 3. **`src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs`** (the `PAGE_ALIGNMENT`
40.    constant model, ~lines 4–11):
41.    - Changed the `ensures` from `result == Alignment::Align4096` to the explicit link
42.      ```rust
43.      ::sys::mm::spec_align_value(result) == spec_page_size()
44.      ```
45.      i.e. "the page alignment's numeric value equals the page size" — true (both 4096 on
46.      the target). This is the `PAGE_ALIGNMENT ↔ spec_page_size()` connection (reviewer's
47.      item 2), stated as an explicit additive fact rather than admitted. It does not pin
48.      `spec_page_size()` to a literal globally; it only equates it to the page alignment's
49.      value where `PAGE_ALIGNMENT` is used.
50. 
51. 4. **`src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.rs`** (`from_address`, ~line 49):
52.    - **Deleted** `proof! { admit(); }`. No replacement proof block was needed — with the
53.      two dependency specs above, Verus discharges all arms automatically:
54.      `is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)` ⇒ `aligned == (addr@ % spec_align_value(PAGE_ALIGNMENT) == 0)`
55.      and `spec_align_value(PAGE_ALIGNMENT) == spec_page_size()`, hence
56.      `aligned == (addr@ % spec_page_size() == 0) == spec_aligned(addr@)`. The `Ok` arm gives
57.      `r@ == addr@` (view = `self.0@`) and `r.inv()`; the `Err` arm gives `!spec_aligned(addr@)`.
58.    - `from_address`'s `ensures` is **unchanged**; no `external_body`/`assume` was introduced.
59. 
60. ### Verification
61. 
62. `make verify-kernel` (module) — exit 0, `from_address` admit removed:
63. ```
64. $ make verify-kernel MODULE=hal::mem::types::address::aligned::page
65.   verification results:: 2 verified, 0 errors (partial verification with `--verify-*`)
66.   Exit code : 0
67.   cheating: assume=0 external_body=14 admit=24 trusted=0 no_decreases=0 cfg_gate=16
68. 
69. $ grep aligned/page verus-ai-logs/verify-kernel/verus-logs/cheating-detail.txt
70.   (no aligned/page entries — 'from_address: admit' is GONE)
71. 
72. $ grep -nE 'admit|assume|external_body|trusted' \
73.     src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.rs \
74.     src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs \
75.     src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.proof.rs
76.   page.spec.rs:7:pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::PAGE_ALIGNMENT ] ...   # constant model only
77. ```
78. 
79. - **admit count: 25 → 24** (the `from_address: admit` line is the one removed). The
80.   remaining 24 `admit` / 14 `external_body` are all pre-existing placeholders in
81.   `mm/phys/*` and the `FrameAddress` shims — none in this module's own functions. The
82.   whole-crate `status: CHEATING_DETECTED` is that pre-existing aggregate, not this module.
83. - The only `assume`/trusted item left in the three module files is the `PAGE_ALIGNMENT`
84.   `assume_specification` constant model, exactly as the reviewer's verify step expects.
85. 
86. `make verify` (full regression) — every crate exit 0:
87. ```
88. bitmap:         70 verified, 0 errors,  Exit code : 0
89. sys:                                     Exit code : 0
90. nanvix-slab:    35 verified, 0 errors,  Exit code : 0
91. bump-allocator:                          Exit code : 0
92. kernel (all):   50 verified, 0 errors,  Exit code : 0
93. ```
94. 
95. `make build` (normal dual compilation):
96. ```
97. $ ./z build -- check-kernel
98.   {"reason":"build-finished","success":true}
99.   [OK]    Build complete.
100. $ ./z build -- check          # host crates (uservm/nanvixd) that depend on sys
101.   {"reason":"build-finished","success":true}
102.   [OK]    Build complete.
103. ```
104. The new `spec_align_value` spec fn and `is_aligned` spec are erased in non-Verus builds
105. (`#[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]` / `#[verus_spec]`), so normal compilation is unaffected.
106. 
107. ### Result: FIXED
108. 
109. `from_address` verifies with **no `admit`** and an **unchanged `ensures`**. The fix
110. strengthened the dependency specs (`Address::is_aligned` contract + a `spec_align_value`
111. accessor + the explicit `PAGE_ALIGNMENT == page size` link) rather than the trust surface;
112. no `external_body`/`assume`/`weaken` was used on the module's own function. `make verify`
113. and both normal builds pass.
